sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
We have measured Basel's garages since 2020. They were quietest in the first lockdown (24% occupied in April 2020), recovered to about 38% in 2022–2024, then fell to about 34% in 2025 and have stayed there in 2026. The fall is not spread across the city. It is almost entirely in the garages by the stations and the exhibition grounds: Centralbahn at Basel SBB went from 33% to 18% on average (January–September 2024 against 2025), the Badischer Bahnhof garage from 66% to 54%, and the Messe garage from 29% to 19%. The central garages barely moved, and Storchen by the Marktplatz gained.

Basel has been making street parking dearer and scarcer for years. Residents' permits doubled to CHF 284 a year in 2019, with one permit per person [0], and in 2021 voters refused to undo the 2019 increase in parking fees [4]. From 2025 permits are priced by car length, CHF 332 to CHF 512 a year, with a further rise announced for 2027 [7]. Meter prices are to be set place by place according to demand, between CHF 1 and CHF 4 an hour [8]. Street spaces fell by about 2,000 to about 26,000 between 2015 and 2024, against about 80,000 spaces on private land including the public garages [13]. The canton's plan is to move street parking into neighbourhood garages [12].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
New capacity has come through garages tied to the removal of street spaces. Parking Kunstmuseum opened at St. Alban-Graben in December 2021 with 350 spaces [5], on condition that 210 street spaces nearby go for good; by mid-2022 only 104 had [6]. In December 2024 the city bought the Horburg garage from Novartis, until then reserved for its staff, and planned to open part of it to long-term renters [10]. Neighbourhood garages are planned in Kleinbasel, partly in the converted Novartis Klybeck garage and in the Messehalle 3 redevelopment [12], and a first pilot was to rent out about 50 private underground spaces through an online platform [11].

The canton's eight garages hold about 4,300 spaces but only about two dozen 22 kW chargers between them [16]; separately, the cantonal parliament funded 200 neighbourhood charging stations by the energy utility IWB [3]. Parking has been payable by app since 2021 [2]. Demand from outside has two sides: Art Basel drew 88,000 visitors in 2025 and about 90,000 in 2026 [14][15], while from 2025 Switzerland halved the duty-free allowance for shopping abroad, a measure aimed at cross-border shopping [9].

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
The canton is the largest garage operator, with City, Steinen, Elisabethen, Storchen and others, and the rest are mostly single private garages. Prices are close together, typically CHF 2.50–3 an hour, and price explains little about which garages fill. The exception is Storchen, right by the Marktplatz, which charges CHF 4 and is one of the busiest (59%).

The busiest garage is the privately run Clarahuus in Kleinbasel (81%), full on weekends too. The Badischer Bahnhof garage behaves like a commuter car park: 68% on weekdays and 17% at weekends. So do Aeschen and Anfos, which empty at weekends. Most central garages run at 25–45% on weekdays and weekends alike, so even in the old town there is usually room; the large City garage is the exception, emptier at weekends (18%).
